oneTimers: Delayed filing: these final figures come from the Form 10-Q filed February 25, 2025 — nearly five months after quarter-end — after EY resigned as auditor on October 24, 2024 and an independent special committee completed its review on December 2, 2024. The quarter was first reported only as preliminary ranges on November 5, 2024 (net sales $5.9–6.0B, non-GAAP diluted EPS $0.75–0.76).

Stock-based compensation was approximately $64.0M in the quarter, per the 10-Q cash flow statement; the November 5, 2024 preliminary release put non-GAAP diluted EPS at $0.75–0.76 versus GAAP $0.67, with the gap mostly stock-based compensation.
otherDetail: Other income of -$10.1M combines $7.2M of other income, net, less $17.4M of interest expense. A separate $0.02M share of loss from an equity investee is shown as equityM. Three customers each accounted for 10% or more of net sales: Customer B 28.7%, Customer A 20.8% and Customer G 11.9%; one supplier (Supplier A) provided 65.1% of purchases. Cash and equivalents were $2,089M at September 30, 2024, up from $1,670M at June 30, 2024, and inventories were $4,931M. A 10-for-1 forward stock split took effect September 30, 2024, and all per-share figures are split-adjusted.

takeaways.text: Net sales hit $5,937M, up from $2,120M a year ago, driven by demand for GPU servers, high-performance computing and rack-scale solutions. Server and storage systems alone were $5,748M, up 192% year over year.
takeaways.title: Sales nearly tripled on AI servers

takeaways.text: Net income was $424M, up 170% from $157M a year ago, and GAAP diluted EPS was $0.67 versus $0.27. Operating income nearly tripled to $509M even as gross margin narrowed to 13.1% from 16.7% a year ago.
takeaways.title: Profit more than doubled

takeaways.text: These final figures landed in the 10-Q on February 25, 2025 — the quarter had only been reported as preliminary ranges on November 5, 2024, after Ernst & Young resigned on October 24, 2024 and a special committee reviewed governance concerns. The committee found no evidence of misconduct, and BDO USA is the new auditor.
takeaways.title: Five months late, after the auditor quit

verdict: Supermicro's sales nearly tripled to $5.9 billion on AI server demand and profit jumped to $424 million — but the final numbers arrived five months late, after its auditor quit.
